title: Customer data migration to a new platform
description: Your team is moving a legacy customer database to a new cloud platform before the old data-centre contract ends. Cutover weekend cannot move.
assumptions: Team of five: three engineers, one database administrator and one analyst, plus a vendor support contract.
Cutover weekend (day 24) is fixed because the old data-centre contract ends then.
The migration tool is supplied by the new platform vendor and cannot be modified.
Measures are health scores from 0 (critical) to 100 (excellent), not literal percentages.
Effects of decisions are simplified training models, not statistical forecasts.
Every measure slowly erodes each day as ordinary project pressure; good decisions offset it.

events.title: Undocumented tables discovered
events.description: Engineers find dozens of tables that appear in no documentation.

events.title: Vendor tool throttles bulk loads
events.description: The migration tool loads data far slower than the vendor promised.

events.title: Audit finds duplicate customers
events.description: A data quality audit finds thousands of duplicate customer records.

events.title: Dry run passes with warnings
events.description: The full dry run completes, with a short list of warnings to review.

events.title: Your DBA has a job offer
events.description: The only database administrator tells you they are considering another job.

events.title: Rehearsal exposes a rollback gap
events.description: The cutover rehearsal shows there is no tested way to roll back if cutover fails.

decisions.prompt: Dozens of undocumented tables turned up. How do you handle them?

options.label: Pause and document every table
options.tradeoff: Thorough and safe, but it uses up days you do not have.

options.label: Sample the tables and keep moving
options.tradeoff: Keeps momentum, but unknown data may bite later.

options.label: Pay the vendor for a discovery workshop
options.tradeoff: Expert help quickly, at a price.

decisions.prompt: Bulk loads are too slow to finish in time. What do you do?

options.label: Run loads in parallel
options.tradeoff: Faster, but more moving parts and more chances for errors.

options.label: Buy extra throughput capacity
options.tradeoff: The simplest fix, paid for in budget.

options.label: Run big batches overnight
options.tradeoff: Uses idle time, but means night work for the team.

decisions.prompt: Thousands of duplicate customers were found. How do you deal with them?

options.label: Clean the data before migrating
options.tradeoff: Best result, but a slow manual effort.

options.label: Migrate as-is and flag duplicates
options.tradeoff: Quick, but the new platform inherits the mess.

options.label: Write an automated dedupe script
options.tradeoff: A good middle path, if the script is right.

decisions.prompt: Your only DBA is thinking of leaving. What do you do?

options.label: Support a retention offer
options.tradeoff: Likely keeps them through cutover, but it is costly.

options.label: Start knowledge transfer now
options.tradeoff: Reduces dependence on one person, but takes time from everyone.

options.label: Assume it will be fine
options.tradeoff: Costs nothing today, and may cost a lot later.

decisions.prompt: There is no tested rollback plan. What do you do with three days left?

options.label: Build and test a rollback
options.tradeoff: Safe, but it uses a lot of the remaining time.

options.label: Accept the risk and keep the date
options.tradeoff: Keeps the schedule intact but cutover becomes a gamble.

options.label: Negotiate a longer cutover window
options.tradeoff: A middle path that costs some money and goodwill.
